# t2.3 — Frontend Advisory Remediation and Build Verification

## Summary
Remediated the critical Next.js npm advisory without changing the Next.js major. The direct framework and lint configuration moved together from `16.3.8` to `16.4.6`, the transitive dependency tree was refreshed, and the final audit is clean. A reusable `npm test` script now runs the existing three Node tests, while runtime validation confirms the production build and home route remain functional.

## Files Changed
- `giro-app/package.json`
  - Upgraded `next` from `16.3.8` to `16.4.6`.
  - Upgraded `eslint-config-next` from `16.3.8` to `16.4.6`.
  - Added `test: node --test lib/*.test.mjs`.
- `giro-app/package-lock.json`
  - Regenerated resolved dependency metadata and audit fixes.
  - Final resolved examples: `typescript-eslint@8.73.0`, `zod@4.6.7`, `minimatch@11.0.9` for the TypeScript ESLint tree, while `eslint` uses its separate deduplicated `minimatch@3.1.5`.
- `giro-app/.tsupgrader/runtime-validation/eval-plan.json`
  - Added deterministic build, existing-test, and `/` HTTP 200 assertions.
- `giro-app/.tsupgrader/runtime-validation/baseline-result.json`
  - Records the pre-upgrade Next `16.3.8` baseline.
- `giro-app/.tsupgrader/runtime-validation/postupgrade-result.json`
  - Records the final Next `16.4.6` validation and zero regressions.

## Dependency and Advisory Results
- Initial audit: 9 vulnerabilities — 1 critical, 1 high, 7 moderate.
- Critical direct dependency: `next@16.3.8`.
- Critical/high patch target: `next@16.4.6`; this remains within Next.js major 16.
- Matched config dependency: `eslint-config-next@16.4.6`.
- Final audit: 0 vulnerabilities — 0 critical, 0 high, 0 moderate, 0 low.
- Final dependency tree verification: `npm ls next eslint-config-next react react-dom zod minimatch typescript --all` exited 0.

The Node test runner emits a non-fatal module-typeless warning while executing the existing `.ts` helper from an `.mjs` test. Test results are still 3/3 passing; no `"type": "module"` package-wide change was introduced because it could affect unrelated runtime behavior.
